note: PI3K-pathway-driven breast lines and xenografts predicted pan-PI3K activity and PIK3CA-mutant enrichment; pictilisib's randomised trials missed PFS with no mutant enrichment, buparlisib's two fulvestrant phase 3s won by about two months and were abandoned for liver and mood toxicity the models never flagged.
label: Breast cancer (pan-PI3K)

engagement.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
engagement.note: GDC-0941 at 150 mg/kg held tumour exposure above antiproliferative levels for >8 h with sustained pathway (pAkt) inhibition in xenografts.
engagement.short: Sustained pAkt inhibition in xenograft tumours
engagement.quote: GDC-0941 showed comparable in vitro antitumor activity to PI-103, PI-540, and PI-620 and exhibited 78% oral bioavailability in mice, with tumor exposure above 50% antiproliferative concentrations for >8 hours following 150 mg/kg p.o. and sustained phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase pathway inhibition.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC2718129 open access). Pivotal preclinical paper for pictilisib; glioblastoma and ovarian xenografts, breast models came with O'Brien 2010.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first use for the class: the model's PD readout is tumour PI3K-pathway (pAkt) inhibition at an exposure above the antiproliferative concentration.

engagement.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
engagement.note: Pictilisib suppressed tumour Ser473-pAkt >90% at exposures above 20 h·µmol/L and PRP pAkt >90% at the MTD; insulin, glucose and FDG-PET moved.
engagement.quote: Levels of phosphorylated serine-473 AKT were suppressed >90% in PRP at 3 hours after dose at the MTD and in tumor at pictilisib doses associated with AUC >20 h·μmol/L.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC4287394 open access). Mixed solid-tumour phase 1 (n=60), not breast-specific; phase 1 NCT not located, so registry_date is null.
engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour pAkt suppression; the model abstract states sustained pathway inhibition without a percentage, patients >90%
engagement.reason: Tumour pAkt suppressed in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: The model's readout (tumour pAkt) moved in dosed humans, so same; the trial is in mixed solid tumours, which the brief allows for engagement. Every member concurs: pilaralisib cut tumour and surrogate pAKT/S6 40-80% (Shapiro 2014, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-13-1777, epub 2013), buparlisib moved skin pS6, C-peptide and FDG-PET dose-dependently (Bendell 2012, doi 10.1200/JCO.2011.36.1360), and in ER+ breast patients pictilisib plus anastrozole suppressed Ki-67 more than anastrozole alone (OPPORTUNE, Schmid 2016, doi 10.1200/JCO.2015.63.9179; downstream). Scored on Sarker 2015 because its model side (Raynaud 2009, same ICR group) is the pivotal preclinical paper; Shapiro 2014 is a year earlier but its model paper (Foster 2015) was published after the trial.

dose.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
dose.note: Exposure target stated: tumour concentration above the 50% antiproliferative level for >8 h after 150 mg/kg oral; no tolerability margin stated.
dose.quote: GDC-0941 showed comparable in vitro antitumor activity to PI-103, PI-540, and PI-620 and exhibited 78% oral bioavailability in mice, with tumor exposure above 50% antiproliferative concentrations for >8 hours following 150 mg/kg p.o. and sustained phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase pathway inhibition.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The abstract reports no body-weight, NOAEL or tolerated-dose statement for mice.
dose.judgement: Opening entry: the model gives an exposure target (tumour level above the antiproliferative concentration with sustained pathway inhibition) but no tolerability margin, so decision 16 cannot be applied on this track.

dose.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
dose.note: FERGI dosed pictilisib at 340 mg, above the 330 mg where tumour pAkt fell >90%; PFS missed, dose cut to 260 mg, program dropped.
dose.quote: Although addition of pictilisib to fulvestrant did not significantly improve progression-free survival, dosing of pictilisib was limited by toxicity, potentially limiting its efficacy.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC5524539). FERGI NCT01437566 has no results posted, so registry_date is null. No exposure-level model-versus-patient comparison was read, so magnitude is null.
dose.reason: Reached, failed, abandoned in this setting
dose.judgement: Part 1 gave 340 mg daily, at or above the 330 mg RP2D where Sarker 2015 showed >90% tumour pAkt suppression, so the model's pathway-inhibition exposure was reached; the primary endpoint missed and Roche stopped pictilisib in this setting, which is the 'reached, failed, abandoned' row (contra derived from efficacy). Part 2's cut to 260 mg for toxicity is not scored as blocked_by because Raynaud 2009 stated no tolerability margin. Buparlisib on the same track would be same: its 100 mg/day MTD showed clear target inhibition (Bendell 2012) and BELLE-2 met its primary at that dose; one drug's contra beats another's same on one track, so it sits in this judgement. PEGGY dosed 260 mg on days 1-5 only, below the daily target, and also failed.

efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
efficacy.note: Breast lines and xenografts with PIK3CA mutation, HER2 amplification or dual pathway lesions were exquisitely sensitive to GDC-0941; some unaltered models responded too.
efficacy.quote: We found that models harboring mutations in PIK3CA, amplification of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, or dual alterations in two pathway components were exquisitely sensitive to the antitumor effects of GDC-0941.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First breast-specific model paper for a member; Wallin 2012 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-2088) added breast xenografts and PDX with docetaxel, Sanchez 2011 (doi 10.1186/bcr2833) BKM120 with oestrogen deprivation in ER+ lines in vitro.
efficacy.population: breast cancer lines and xenografts, PI3K-pathway-altered and unaltered
efficacy.judgement: Class-level opening entry in the breast models (the track's first use was Raynaud 2009 in non-breast xenografts, proxy allowed).

efficacy.model: Breast cancer cell-line panel with genotype: PIK3CA-mutant and HER2-amplified lines most sensitive
efficacy.note: Pharmacogenomic profiling of a large breast-line panel proposed PIK3CA mutation, HER2 amplification and a gene signature to pick responders.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA/HER2 status proposed to pick responders
efficacy.quote: Pathway focused biomarkers and the gene expression signature described in this study may have utility in the identification of patients likely to benefit from therapy with a selective PI3K inhibitor.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Maira 2012 (doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-11-0474) made the same prediction for buparlisib from a 353-line panel (preferential inhibition of PIK3CA-mutant lines).
efficacy.judgement: A separate track: a different prediction (which patients respond) from a genotype-annotated line panel, not the class-level xenograft question. model_kind is animal because the panel paper also carried xenografts; the genotype call itself is in vitro.

efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
efficacy.note: FERGI: pictilisib plus fulvestrant did not improve PFS (6.6 vs 5.1 months, HR 0.74, p=0.096) in AI-resistant ER+ breast cancer.
efficacy.quote: In part 1, we found no difference in median progression-free survival between the pictilisib (6·6 months [95% CI 3·9-9·8]) and placebo (5·1 months [3·6-7·3]) group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·74 [95% CI 0·52-1·06]; p=0·096).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC5524539). NCT01437566 has no results posted; year is the 2016-05-04 epub. BELLE-2 was presented at SABCS 2015 but its first admissible record is the 2017 paper.

patient_trials.quote: In the ITT population, the median PFS was 8.2 months with pictilisib (n = 91) versus 7.8 months with placebo (n = 92) [hazard ratio (HR) for progression or death, 0.95; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.62-1.46; P = 0.83].

In the total patient population (n=1147), median progression-free survival was 6·9 months (95% CI 6·8-7·8) in the buparlisib group versus 5·0 months (4·0-5·2) in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·78 [95% CI 0·67-0·89]; one-sided p=0·00021).

Median progression-free survival was significantly longer in the buparlisib versus placebo group (3·9 months [95% CI 2·8-4·2] vs 1·8 months [1·5-2·8]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·67, 95% CI 0·53-0·84, one-sided p=0·00030).

At adaptive interim analysis, there was no improvement in PFS with buparlisib versus placebo in the full (median PFS 8.0 versus 9.2 months, hazard ratio [HR] 1.18), or PI3K pathway-activated population (median PFS 9.1 versus 9.2 months, HR 1.17).
Overall, pCR rate was similar between buparlisib and placebo arms (32.0% versus 40%; one-sided P = 0.811).
Fifty-one patients were enrolled in phase II; one patient had a partial response in the pilaralisib arm.
No responses occurred in Arm 1; four of 20 evaluable patients (20 %) in Arm 2 had a partial response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft growth inhibition versus PFS HR 0.74, p=0.096 (not significant)
efficacy.reason: Pictilisib failed; buparlisib wins cannot flip
efficacy.judgement: Class-level call on one track. Pictilisib, the drug the model was built on, missed its PFS primary in FERGI and PEGGY, and the discovery paper's own pitch (potentiating taxanes, Wallin 2012) failed in PEGGY. Buparlisib plus fulvestrant then met PFS primaries in BELLE-2 (HR 0.78, +1.9 months) and BELLE-3 (HR 0.67, +2.1 months), which read as same with source_calls_it partial, but BELLE-4 (paclitaxel) stopped for futility, NeoPHOEBE (HER2+) missed pCR, pilaralisib gave 1 PR of 51 with letrozole and 0 of 21 with trastuzumab alone, and Novartis abandoned buparlisib for toxicity. Under the rule that one drug's contra beats another's same on a track, the track stays contra; a reviewer who treats the Genentech and Novartis model programs as separate systems would draw buparlisib's as same/partial. OPPORTUNE (Ki-67 primary, positive) is a PD window study, scored under engagement.

efficacy.model: Breast cancer cell-line panel with genotype: PIK3CA-mutant and HER2-amplified lines most sensitive
efficacy.note: FERGI: PIK3CA-mutant patients gained nothing over wild-type (HR 0.73 vs 0.72), and the mutant-only part 2 showed HR 1.07.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA mutation did not enrich benefit
efficacy.quote: We also found no difference when patients were analysed according to presence (pictilisib 6·5 months [95% CI 3·7-9·8] vs placebo 5·1 months [2·6-10·4]; HR 0·73 [95% CI 0·42-1·28]; p=0·268)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Quote is a verbatim leading fragment of the abstract's PIK3CA sentence. Same-year earlier signals: OPPORTUNE (epub 2016-03-14) found PIK3CA mutations not predictive of Ki-67 response, and the buparlisib phase 1s (Bendell 2012, Rodon 2014) saw no correlation of tumour molecular status with benefit.

patient_trials.quote: In patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumours, the median PFS was 7.3 months for pictilisib (n = 32) versus 5.8 months with placebo (n = 30) (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.52-2.12; P = 0.88).

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).
There was no association between molecular alterations in the PI3K pathway and efficacy.
Observed PIK3CA mutations in cell-free circulating DNA did not correlate with response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.73 in PIK3CA-mutant versus 0.72 in wild-type: no enrichment
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction tested on its own drug: the panel said PIK3CA-mutant tumours are exquisitely sensitive, and the stratified, then mutant-only, FERGI showed no enrichment. PEGGY (HR 1.06 mutant), pilaralisib (no association, two trials) and BELLE-4 (HR 1.17 pathway-activated) agree. BELLE-2's tissue-defined pathway-activated group (HR 0.76 vs 0.78 overall) adds nothing, and its ctDNA PIK3CA-mutant exploratory signal (HR 0.56) and BELLE-3's are partial matches on another drug that cannot flip a contra track.

efficacy.model: Breast cancer patient-derived tumour xenograft (PDTX) biobank with short-term PDTX-derived tumour cell (PDTC) ex vivo drug screen (Cambridge; pictilisib ex vivo, buparlisib in vivo)
efficacy.note: PDTC screen of pictilisib across 15 models: sensitivity sat with PIK3CA-activating mutation, PTEN loss, INPP4B loss or high p-AKT; buparlisib dosed in PDTXs in vivo.
efficacy.short: PDTC screen ties pictilisib sensitivity to PIK3CA/PTEN
efficacy.quote: Sensitivity to the PI3Kα inhibitor GDC00941 (pictilisib) was seen in models with PIK3CA-activating mutations (3/15), PTEN loss (5/15), INPP4B loss (2/15), high p-AKT levels (4/15), or a combination of these features
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5037319, open access). The paper pairs no PI3K-inhibitor result with a patient: the biobank's patients were not treated with class members. model_kind is ex_vivo because the scored pictilisib screen is in PDTCs; the same biobank also dosed buparlisib in PDTXs in vivo (Table S7, numbers not quotable from the text).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the biobank's first published use. Patient-level prediction (which genotypes respond to pictilisib); the paper itself makes no comparison with patients.
efficacy.population: Breast cancer PDTX/PDTC models (n = 15 screened with pictilisib), ER+ and ER- mixed

efficacy.model: Breast cancer patient-derived tumour xenograft (PDTX) biobank with short-term PDTX-derived tumour cell (PDTC) ex vivo drug screen (Cambridge; pictilisib ex vivo, buparlisib in vivo)
efficacy.note: PDTCs said PIK3CA-mutant tumours respond better to pictilisib; FERGI's PIK3CA-mutant patients gained nothing over wild-type (HR 0.73 vs 0.72) and PEGGY agreed (HR 1.06).
efficacy.short: PIK3CA-mutant enrichment not seen in FERGI
efficacy.quote: We also found no difference when patients were analysed according to presence (pictilisib 6·5 months [95% CI 3·7-9·8] vs placebo 5·1 months [2·6-10·4]; HR 0·73 [95% CI 0·42-1·28]; p=0·268)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Bruna 2016 full text (model side, 'models with mutant versus wild-type PIK3CA responded better to PI3Kα and AKT inhibitors') against the FERGI paper (abstract-level; PMC5524539). Dating: FERGI was public before Bruna (SABCS 2014; epub 2016-05-04 vs 2016-09-15), but Bruna does not cite FERGI and the screen date is not stated, so retrodiction is left false; the status is contra under either reading. NCT01437566 has no results posted.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction tested on its own drug: the ex-vivo screen put pictilisib sensitivity with PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss; the stratified, then mutant-only, FERGI showed no enrichment, and PEGGY (HR 1.06) agreed. BELLE-2's tissue-defined PI3K-pathway-activated group (HR 0.76 vs 0.78 overall) adds nothing for buparlisib, and its ctDNA PIK3CA signal is a partial match on another drug that cannot flip a contra track. One drug's contra beats another's same on the same track.
efficacy.reason: Ex-vivo genotype call missed in patients

patient_trials.quote: In patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumours, the median PFS was 7.3 months for pictilisib (n = 32) versus 5.8 months with placebo (n = 30) (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.52-2.12; P = 0.88).

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.73 in PIK3CA-mutant versus 0.72 in wild-type (FERGI part 1), HR 1.07 in the mutant-only part 2: no enrichment
efficacy.population: ER+/HER2-negative, aromatase-inhibitor-resistant advanced breast cancer; PIK3CA-mutant versus wild-type (FERGI, PEGGY)

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX Encyclopedia 1x1x1 'PDX clinical trial' (~1,000 PDXs, six indications; buparlisib-treated PDXs stratified by PAM50 luminal A, PIK3CA and MAP3K1 status)
efficacy.note: Population-scale PDX screen of 62 treatments, buparlisib among them, built to predict clinical trial response; no breast-cancer pan-PI3K comparison verifiable from the abstract.
efficacy.short: PDX 'clinical trial' built to predict response
efficacy.quote: We demonstrate both the reproducibility and the clinical translatability of this approach by identifying associations between a genotype and drug response, and established mechanisms of resistance.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading: nature.com redirects to login and the Firecrawl scrape returned only abstract and references, so whether Gao 2015 itself pairs BKM120 breast-PDX responses with a trial is unverified. Buparlisib's place in the screen is confirmed by Nixon 2019, which analyses 170 buparlisib-treated PDXs from this database (its reference 22).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the PDX encyclopedia's first published use; the first verifiable comparison for a class member in breast cancer comes in Nixon 2019.
efficacy.population: PDXs across six solid-tumour indications including breast; buparlisib single agent

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX Encyclopedia 1x1x1 'PDX clinical trial' (~1,000 PDXs, six indications; buparlisib-treated PDXs stratified by PAM50 luminal A, PIK3CA and MAP3K1 status)
efficacy.note: After luminal A tracked with clinical benefit on buparlisib + letrozole, the 170 buparlisib-treated PDXs were re-stratified: luminal A predicted response; PIK3CA mutation did not, matching the clinic.
efficacy.short: PDX re-analysis reproduces luminal A benefit
efficacy.quote: However, luminal A status predicted response to both drugs, albeit with a greater number of PDXs harboring luminal A gene expression than having alterations in PIK3CA or MAP3K1.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6757060, open access). Weak on both sides: 14 buparlisib patient tumours with PAM50 (3/3 with clinical benefit luminal A), significance only as a trend (p = 0.07) pooled with alpelisib, which is not a class member; the 170 PDXs span solid-tumour types, not breast alone, with n = 1 per model. NCT01248494 has no results posted.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the luminal A hypothesis came from the patients and the PDX database was then queried 'to provide additional evidence', so the model was run against a known answer. It reproduced the direction (luminal A better on buparlisib) and also reproduced the PIK3CA non-enrichment ('PDXs with MAP3K1 alterations were more sensitive to alpelisib ... but not buparlisib'; PIK3CA-mutant PDXs trended only for alpelisib), consistent with FERGI, PEGGY and BELLE-2 tissue results. Scored retro, not same; counted apart.
efficacy.reason: Model reran against known clinic answer

patient_trials.quote: Interestingly, all three patients with clinical benefit to buparlisib/letrozole had a luminal A-like gene expression pattern in their cancer.
Patients harboring mutations in both genes exhibited the greatest likelihood of clinical benefit.

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX day-28 tumour-volume change by luminal A status versus clinical benefit rate (CR/PR or SD >= 6 months) by luminal A status on buparlisib + letrozole
efficacy.population: ER+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer on buparlisib + letrozole phase Ib (NCT01248494), n = 14 with PAM50 subtype; PDX panel across solid-tumour types

safety.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
safety.note: Mice dosed 150 mg/kg daily to 98% growth inhibition; the abstract makes no tolerability statement.
safety.quote: These properties led to excellent dose-dependent oral antitumor activity, with daily p.o. dosing at 150 mg/kg achieving 98% and 80% growth inhibition of U87MG glioblastoma and IGROV-1 ovarian cancer xenografts, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no body-weight, glucose or toxicity statement in the abstract.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: no tolerability prediction to score.

safety.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
safety.note: Novartis stated buparlisib's preclinical safety profile supported clinical development; this is the track's only stated tolerability claim.
safety.quote: The pharmacological, biologic, and preclinical safety profile of NVP-BKM120 supports its clinical development and the compound is undergoing phase II clinical trials in patients with cancer.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the species and findings of the preclinical safety package are not in the abstract and no FDA review exists for any member.
safety.population: mechanistic xenografts (A2780, U87MG) and a 353-line panel
safety.judgement: Same status, kept as a strengthening entry because it is the stated prediction the 2017 entry scores against.

safety.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4)
safety.note: BELLE-2: grade 3-4 ALT rise 25% vs 1%, AST 18% vs 3%; with mood disorders this toxicity ended buparlisib despite a positive primary.
safety.short: Liver toxicity unflagged by preclinical package
safety.quote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events in the buparlisib group versus the placebo group were increased alanine aminotransferase (146 [25%] of 573 patients vs six [1%] of 570), increased aspartate aminotransferase (103 [18%] vs 16 [3%])
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC5549667). Quote is a verbatim leading fragment of the abstract's adverse-event sentence. NCT01610284 results posted 2020-06-18, after the paper. Whether Novartis' rat or dog toxicology showed transaminase rises is unverified; if it did, the harm was predicted and belongs in dose as a misplaced margin, not here.
safety.reason: Hepatotoxicity ended a drug the package cleared
safety.judgement: Scored on the harm the species could have shown: rodents and dogs can show transaminase elevation, the discovery paper called the preclinical safety profile supportive, and grade 3-4 ALT rises hit a quarter of BELLE-2 patients, liver toxicity suspended NeoPHOEBE, and BELLE-2 concluded no further studies would be pursued because of toxicity. Mood alteration, a buparlisib DLT from the phase 1 (Bendell 2012) that drove the discontinuations, is not scored: a xenograft study cannot show it. Hyperglycaemia is on-target and was read as target modulation in the phase 1s, so it is not a miss. Pictilisib's rash DLT (Sarker 2015) and 61% grade 3 or worse events in FERGI part 1 are class-consistent silence on this track; pilaralisib's DLTs were rash and hypersensitivity. Counted once, here, because no member's model predicted it.
